text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

## Abstract
This query tested whether two GEO accessions, GSE309890 and GDS309890, refer to the same record. I queried GEO metadata for both accessions and resolved their accession-to-UID mapping. The records were not the same object: GSE309890 is a GEO Series (entry type GSE) with UID 200309890, while GDS309890 is a GEO DataSet (entry type GDS) with UID 309890. They also have different GEO page URLs and different FTP directory locations. GEO’s accession scheme encodes record type, so the shared numeric suffix does not indicate identity. This matters because a Series and a DataSet can describe related content at different levels of curation and may not carry the same sample set, processed matrix, or metadata completeness. The result resolves the ambiguity directly from GEO rather than by inference.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** GEO uses distinct accession prefixes for different record types, including GSE for Series and GDS for curated DataSets.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** It was unclear whether the two accessions with the same numeric suffix represented the same GEO record.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Determine whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 are identical GEO entries. The hypothesis was that they are different record types and therefore not the same thing.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** I used GEO record lookup and accession resolution to compare the two accessions directly.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO via `geo_series`; NCBI GEO accession resolver via `geo_resolve_accession`.

**Procedures.**  
1. `geo_series({"accession":"GSE309890","list_files":false})`  
2. `geo_series({"accession":"GDS309890","list_files":false})`  
3. `geo_resolve_accession({"accessions":"GSE309890 GDS309890"})`

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistical analysis was performed. Identity was assessed by accession type, resolved UID, and GEO URL/FTP directory equality.

## III. Results
**Data Presentation.**

| Accession | GEO entry type | UID | GEO URL | FTP directory |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| GSE309890 | GSE / Series | 200309890 | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ |
| GDS309890 | GDS / DataSet | 309890 | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/ |

**Findings.** The two accessions are not the same record. They differ in GEO record type, UID, GEO page URL, and FTP directory. The accession resolver reported the rule: UID = type digit + accession number padded to 8 digits; GPL=1, GSE=2, GSM=3, and GDS takes no digit.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct GEO entries, not alternate names for the same record.

**Context.** The retrieved GSE record describes a Series titled “Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback,” while the GDS record is a separate curated DataSet accession with no metadata returned in the summary call.

**Limitations.** The GDS lookup returned minimal metadata in this tool result, so this comparison establishes non-identity but not whether the two entries are biologically related. The GEO API summary also does not provide processed expression values; those remain in supplementary files.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** They are different GEO record types and should not be treated as the same dataset. A useful next query would be to check whether GDS309890 is derived from, summarizes, or references GSE309890 by linking their associated records and supplementary files.

## References
[1] GEO — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890  

## Acknowledgments
Data provided by NCBI GEO.
